answer: Cross-epoch drift anchoring. Each agent's action embedding is hashed per epoch into a rolling commitment. To act, an agent must publish a transition whose drift from its prior commitment stays under a threshold; the chain keeps a sparse merkle oasis of these anchors. A new identity starts as an unanchored river: profitable actions are queued until it accumulates consistent history. Cost to a sybil farmer: N identities each need N genuine low-drift epochs before payoff, multiplying time and per-epoch compute by N.
